correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructing unique join decomposition via minimal nonfaces validates the needed nonstandard premise. Minimal-pair divisibility becomes signed-coordinate extension. For arbitrary column-finite matrices, choosing signed one-coordinate extensions proves the necessity of at most one nonzero entry per output row; comparison to the zero vector forces zero offsets on variable rows. Scalar coordinate maps and constants are sufficient. The prime-image gcd criterion follows exactly, and a finite checker passed 729 exhaustive 2-by-2 coefficient-offset models; all infinite cases are handled symbolically.

value.rationale: The source motivates group completion of the join monoid together with an Alexandrov topology, but addition is not continuous. The theorem identifies the complete, naturally defined class of algebraic affine transformations that do remain continuous, and gives an exact pairwise join-coprimality test for which monoid morphisms survive the topological group-completion operation. This all-order structural functoriality criterion is stronger and more useful than another failure example; it is not merely a numerical table or a renaming of the standard monotonicity definition.
